import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Normality of mathematical constants

Despite extensive empirical evidence—billions of digits have been computed for $\pi$,
$e$, and $\sqrt{2}$, all showing near-uniform digit distribution—it is an open problem
whether any of the classical constants $\pi$, $e$, $\sqrt{2}$, $\ln 2$, or $\varphi$ is
normal in any base.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia (Normal number)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
* [Wikipedia (Pi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi)
-/

open Real

namespace NormalNumber

/--
$\pi$ is normal in base 10.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem pi_normal_base_ten : IsNormalInBase 10 π := by
  sorry

end NormalNumber

findings.description: The theorem states only simple normality of π in base 10, rather than normality. Its imported predicate `NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/NumberTheory/NormalNumber.lean, lines 63–69) quantifies over individual digits `d < b` and requires each digit's frequency to tend to `1 / b`. It never tests longer digit blocks. This is strictly weaker: x = 123456789 / 9999999999 = 0.01234567890123456789… satisfies the exact current predicate in base 10, but the block `00` has frequency zero instead of 1/100. This separation was proved in the scratch Lean file.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number explicitly distinguishes 'simply normal' (each digit has natural density 1/b) from 'normal in base b' (for every positive integer n, all strings of length n have density b^(-n)); its Definitions section gives both frequency formulas. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi#Irrationality_and_normality describes normality as requiring 'all possible sequences of digits (of any given length)' to appear equally often and states the conjecture that π is normal.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the existing condition under a name such as `IsSimplyNormalInBase`, and redefine `IsNormalInBase b x` to quantify over every positive length ℓ and every word `w : Fin ℓ → Fin b`. Require the proportion of starting positions `k < n` satisfying `∀ i : Fin ℓ, digitSeq b x (k + i.val) = (w i).val` to tend to `1 / (b : ℝ)^ℓ`. The theorem should then use this full block-normality predicate. Equivalently, normality in base 10 can be expressed by requiring the existing single-digit condition in every base `10^k`, for every positive integer k.

review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and its shared definitions, including digit extraction, casts, digit bounds, fractional-part conventions, and the empty-prefix value at n = 0. Omitting the integer part and totalizing division at n = 0 do not affect the limiting frequencies. Both cited sources still record π's normality as open. `/workspace/review/counterexample.lean` compiles and proves that the periodic decimal satisfies the imported predicate but not an all-blocks normality predicate; `#print axioms` confirms no dependency on `sorryAx`. The reviewed repository files were not modified.

not_demonstrated.reason: The formalized statement asserts simple normality of π, which is itself open; the defect does not make it trivially provable or refutable. The earlier concrete counterexample to the shared definition has a compiled 96-line proof involving digit periodicity, counting congruence classes, and limits. That exceeds the requested trivial demonstration, and checking finitely many digits would not establish the required asymptotic frequencies.

submission.summary: No trivial_proof.lean file is present. The longer, previously compiled counterexample remains in /workspace/review/counterexample.lean, but is not being presented as a trivial proof.
submission.gave_up_reason: I do not have a handful-line, honest demonstration of the reported weakening. Proving or refuting simple normality of π remains out of reach, and the definition-level counterexample requires substantive periodicity and limit arguments.

submission.summary: Changed the theorem to require the existing single-digit frequency predicate in every base 10^k for k > 0, a standard equivalent characterization of normality in base 10. Updated the docstring to explain this characterization. Only the permitted file was edited, and the required compilation succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Normality of mathematical constants

Despite extensive empirical evidence—billions of digits have been computed for $\pi$,
$e$, and $\sqrt{2}$, all showing near-uniform digit distribution—it is an open problem
whether any of the classical constants $\pi$, $e$, $\sqrt{2}$, $\ln 2$, or $\varphi$ is
normal in any base.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia (Normal number)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
* [Wikipedia (Pi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi)
-/

open Real

namespace NormalNumber

/--
$\pi$ is normal in base 10. Equivalently, it is simply normal in base $10^k$
for every positive integer $k$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem pi_normal_base_ten :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → IsNormalInBase (10 ^ k) π := by
  sorry

end NormalNumber
